prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1439; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the insured reports the other driver was at fault.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with the policy period noted.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both describe the same sequence of events. A witness at the scene also confirmed the impact happened as the insured described.

Entry 4: Inspected the insured vehicle. The rear bumper, trunk lid and tail light damage is consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from the records reviewed.

Entry 5: Claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the collision.

Entry 6: Claimant did not provide a name to anyone at the scene, and the claimant first came into the claim several days after the accident. The claim file was opened on the basis of the insured's report and the other driver's statement.

Entry 7: Medical records reviewed. The wrist fracture is consistent with the type and force of a rear-end impact. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the records obtained so far.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with follow-up visits spaced out as healing progressed. Treatment has tapered off as the claimant improved, and the provider's notes reflect steady recovery.

Entry 9: Claimant's counsel provided an updated account that adds a few small details not in the first statement. The core account of the collision is unchanged from the original report.

Entry 10: File reviewed. Liability and vehicle damage remain consistent with the reported loss, and the injury treatment is progressing as expected. Next step is to continue evaluating the bodily injury component through counsel.
